methodological_questions: Does adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predict series win after controlling for pre-series team strength?
Is the unit of analysis (54 series) large enough to detect an adherence effect on a binary series outcome?
Can adherence be measured out-of-sample, without outcome-derived labels or same-series information?
Is the recommended mix itself valid, or is any observed association produced by label construction or confounding?

historical_evidence.finding: Holdout games where a team's play-type mix is closer to the model's recommended mix score more efficiently: raw gap +5.18 ORtg; strength-controlled gap +3.27 ORtg (+0.0193 vs -0.0134 PPP residual) on 908 holdout game-team rows (454 games). Validation recorded only as same_pipeline_validation; no CI stated.

All BEST vs constrained league mix gap +0.269 (p=0.0000, n=283), but this is CUT-driven. Non-CUT BEST vs mix gap +0.010 (p=0.1709, n=136); L3 matchup non-CUT gap +0.001 (p=0.3277, n=47). Recorded as an adequately powered null for the matchup-specific claim.

Three-level counter ranking (population vs team vs matchup): best counter after a suppressed play type was not stable across levels in the recorded L1/L2 comparison (e.g., L2 MIA disagrees with L1 on DRIVE). Playoff n_matchups 4 to 44; validation not recorded.
SPOT_UP showed 2.83 PPP and TRANSITION 0.62 PPP because the assisted flag exists only on makes; after rewrite SPOT_UP about 1.16 and TRANSITION about 1.20. Recorded as C_artifact.
On-ball defensive scheme labels (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) were labelled at 14.9% (DET, 10 of 67) and 3.3% (ORL, 2 of 60); switches_on not populated. Verdict failed_gate.

Inferred defensive scheme change: within-game 61.0% and cross-game 67.7% change rates; 99.0% of units show a change; transition matrices near-uniform, consistent with label noise. Doc caveat: inferred labels cannot separate defensive adjustment from offense executing differently.
Single WCF Game 5 replay: CUT opener high-PPP on tiny volume (SAS n=9, OKC n=1); one game only.
Observed vs recommended mix conformance in 4 single 2025-26 playoff G1s; avg |delta| 4.5 to 24.0pp; CUT and PNR muted for tagger floor; no outcome comparison.
Season adapter profiles: team BEST share is descriptive; win% not identified with BEST share (e.g., IND 4.5% BEST, 71% win; DEN 4.9% BEST, 62% win). No inferential test of stability vs noise.
2024-25 playoff PNR proxy calibration coverage: 62 of 85 games in graph, 0 errors; tool evaluation pass. Not an outcome test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Matchup-specific non-CUT BEST counters beating a feasibility-weighted league mix
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as B_powered_null: non-CUT gap +0.010, p=0.1709 (n=136); the headline effect is CUT-driven; LIM:selection_or_regression_to_the_mean and LIM:small_sample recorded.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Stable counter ranking across population, team and matchup levels
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as inconclusive with LIM:small_sample and RISK:MECHANICAL_FLOOR; L1 n_mu as low as 5; L2 disagrees with L1 on DRIVE.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type classification used to produce possession-level PPP
failed_approaches.why: C_artifact: assisted flag present only on makes inflated SPOT_UP PPP to 2.83; the labelling flaw was identified and rewritten.

failed_approaches.what_failed: On-ball coverage label (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) from NBA matchup/PBP fields
failed_approaches.why: Label rates too low for use (14.9% DET, 3.3% ORL); switches_on not populated; A_unanswerable with LIM:label_or_classification_error and LIM:small_sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferred scheme-change labels as evidence of defensive adaptation
failed_approaches.why: A_unanswerable: label cannot separate defensive change from offensive execution; near-uniform transition matrices suggest label noise.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Single-game replay of the LP opener vs realized mix
failed_approaches.why: A_unanswerable: one game, tiny volume for the opener (SAS n=9, OKC n=1).

evidence_establishes: A game-level, holdout-based association between closeness to a recommended play-type mix and efficiency exists in one pipeline (FAM:SF-APPM-001), after team/opponent residualization.
Matchup-specific counter claims were not supported once CUT-driven gains were removed, at the powered non-CUT scale (FAM:SF-APPS-023).
Defensive scheme labels derived from play-by-play are unreliable at usable rates (FAM:SF-APPS-058, FAM:SF-APPA-005).
Play-type labels can carry construction artifacts that create spurious efficiency gaps (FAM:SF-PAP-096), so labels must be audited before any mix-based inference.
evidence_does_not_establish: Anything about series-level winning. No retrieved record tests series win as the outcome; FAM:SF-APPM-001 uses game-team efficiency (PPP/ORtg).
Whether a suppression-conditional recommendation is valid as a prescription; the closest records measure association with efficiency, not causal effect of adherence.
Whether adherence is distinct from team quality; FAM:SF08 explicitly found win% not identified with BEST share.
Any result on the 2025-26 playoffs, which were partial as of 2026-06-16 and are not in the retrieved records.
Power for a 54-series binary test; no retrieved record reports a series-level analysis.
own_inferences: Fifty-four series give only about 54 independent binary outcomes. Detecting a modest adherence effect on series win would need far more series than are available, so the test is likely underpowered even if the label is valid.
Using play-by-play to define both the recommended mix (from suppression states) and the adherence measure risks outcome leakage if points or game state from the same series enter the recommendation.
A plausible design exists at game level (about 5 games per series), with series-clustered inference, but adherence must be frozen before each game and team strength controlled from pre-series data.
The question as posed (predicts winning) conflates game-level efficiency with series outcome, which is a change of estimand.
uncertainties: The retrieved records do not show a series-level analysis, so their effect sizes may not transfer to series win probability.
FAM:SF-APPM-001 reports no CI and only same-pipeline validation; its robustness to label revision is unknown.
The exact definition of 'suppression-conditional' and of adherence is not in the retrieved records; the record set may not be complete.
The 2025-26 playoff data were partial on 2026-06-16; the 54-series count may change once the season completes on 2026-06-21.
Tagger floors (FAM:SF-APPS-017) may cap the number of play types that can be measured reliably, limiting adherence scoring.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieved evidence showed the main risks (label error, artifacts, low-power nulls, confounding by strength) and that the closest positive result (FAM:SF-APPM-001) is at game-efficiency level, not series win. This moved the decision from a direct series-win test to a not-yet proceed with a restructured, pre-registered game-level design.

blocking_constraints.text: 54 series give roughly 54 independent binary outcomes; power for a modest adherence effect on series win is very low.
Adherence and the recommended mix are built from play-by-play points, which are also the outcome basis; a leak-free out-of-sample construction is required.
Play-type and scheme labels show artifacts and poor coverage (FAM:SF-PAP-096, FAM:SF-APPS-058); reliability of adherence is unverified.
Team quality drives both adherence and wins; FAM:SF08 shows win% is not identified with BEST share.

prior_work.summary: Earlier work addressed related questions: a game-level holdout association between mix alignment and efficiency was supported with strength control (FAM:SF-APPM-001). Matchup-specific counter advantages were a powered null beyond CUT (FAM:SF-APPS-023). Counter rankings were inconclusive across levels (FAM:SF-APPM-055). No retrieved work tests series-level win as the outcome of adherence.

risks.text: 54 series; binary outcome; low power for any realistic effect.
Recommended mix and adherence derived from the same play-by-play used for outcomes.
Recommendation must be frozen before the series; in-series information must not enter adherence or recommendation.
Team strength and opponent quality confound adherence and wins.
Defensive scheme labels show low coverage and near-uniform transitions (FAM:SF-APPS-058, FAM:SF-APPA-005).
Tagger floors mute CUT and PNR (FAM:SF-APPS-017, FAM:SF-APPM-055).
A positive result may depend on the recommendation construction; placebo mixes are needed.
Multiple recommended-mix variants and play-type splits create multiple-comparison risk.
Play-type and coaching patterns change across seasons (FAM:SF08); pooled seasons may mix regimes.
Series win base rate near 50% for matched teams; small effects are hard to distinguish from noise.
Play-type classifier rewrites have already produced artifacts (FAM:SF-PAP-096).

design.estimand: Within-series association between pre-registered, out-of-sample adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix and game-level win, conditional on pre-series team strength (not series win as posed).
design.unit: Team-game within series, with series as the cluster; series outcome reported as secondary.
design.sample: 2022-23 through 2024-25 playoffs (complete) for development; 2025-26 playoffs held out and used only after freezing the recommended mix; exclude 2025-26 games not complete as of the freeze date.
design.power: Given 54 series, the primary test is underpowered for series win; power must be computed on game-level clustered variance before running. If power is below 0.8 for the pre-specified minimum effect, do not claim a result.
design.controls: Pre-series team strength (prior-season net rating or Elo), opponent strength, home court, rest; recommended mix fit only on prior seasons; adherence computed with labels that avoid outcome points.
design.falsification: Placebo recommended mix (mix from a random other team or a shuffled state-to-play map) must show null association; a pre-specified negative-control outcome (e.g., regular-season non-playoff games) must show no association.
design.multiplicity: One pre-registered primary coefficient (adherence on game win, strength-controlled); all other splits and variants labelled exploratory with Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Claim support only if the primary coefficient is positive with a series-clustered 95% CI excluding zero, the placebo is null, and the effect survives strength control; otherwise report as rejected or uncertain.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs; 2025-26 playoffs frozen at completion (2026-06-21); 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13 only; pin label version and classifier commit.

methodological_questions: does adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predict series outcome
sample size and unit of analysis for series-level outcomes (54 series)
label leakage from play-by-play derived possession points
confounding by team quality and opponent strength
validity of recommended-mix construction and placebo tests
args.query: defensive suppression counter strategy recommended play mix adherence predicts winning series outcome NBA playoffs

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Field guidance:
- historical_evidence and failed_approaches: only records returned by a tool, with the status as recorded; empty lists
  if nothing relevant was returned.
- testability.p_testable: probability that the question can be answered with the stated data at useful statistical power.
- prior_work.already_answered: whether retrieved earlier work already answered substantially the same question.
  Use "unknown" if no earlier work was retrieved. List identifiers you relied on in prior_work.cited.
- predicted_outcome: probabilities (summing to 1) of what a competent test of the question as posed would conclude:
  supported, rejected (adequately powered null), untestable (cannot be tested with this data), artifact (apparent
  effect produced by a flaw), uncertain (inconclusive or inadequately tested).
- decision: proceed, proceed_with_changes (state the changes in design), or do_not_proceed.
- design: a pre-registration-quality plan even if the decision is do_not_proceed (then describe the minimum viable test).
